name: Source Attribution
summary: Link generated content back to its sources—retrieved documents, web pages, citations—so users can verify claims and judge reliability.
problem: Generated responses cite sources or claim knowledge but provide no way for users to verify those sources. Users cannot distinguish between retrieval-grounded facts and hallucinations, and cannot judge the credibility of the source.
useWhen: The response is grounded in retrieved documents or external data
Users need to verify claims or audit the model's reasoning
The sources are publicly accessible and verifiable
dontUseWhen: Sources are proprietary, internal, or cannot be shared
The response is pure reasoning or generation with no retrieval component
Source links would be overwhelming or distract from the response

anatomy.description: The text or phrase within the response that is cited; highlighted or numbered.
A clickable, keyboard-accessible link to the source document, page, or data.
Title, author, publication date, and domain of the source; shown on hover or in a modal.
A consolidated list of all sources at the end of the response for batch inspection.

states.description: Content with one or more sources linked.
User has expanded a source to see metadata or full context.
A source link is dead or inaccessible.

constraints.statement: Every citation anchor MUST be keyboard-accessible and clickable, not just hover-based.
constraints.rationale: Keyboard and mobile users must be able to reach citations without a pointing device.
constraints.verification: E2E test: Tab to citation anchor and activate via Enter; assert source opens.

constraints.statement: A citation MUST link to a source that is publicly accessible and can be independently verified.
constraints.rationale: Citations to inaccessible or private sources are worse than no citation; they mislead users into trusting unverifiable claims.
constraints.verification: Code review: verify all source URLs are public and valid; periodically audit links for rot.

constraints.statement: Citations MUST be visually distinct from surrounding text and communicable via assistive technology; color alone is insufficient.
constraints.rationale: Color-blind and screen reader users must perceive citations and be able to reach them.
constraints.verification: Automated a11y test: citation anchors carry a non-color affordance (marker glyph or superscript number) and an accessible name; axe check passes.

constraints.statement: Source metadata (title, author, date, domain) SHOULD be available without leaving the page, via tooltip, modal, or adjacent panel.
constraints.rationale: Users need to judge source credibility before leaving the page; metadata reduces friction.
constraints.verification: Manual review: activate a citation anchor and confirm source metadata is reachable without page navigation.

constraints.statement: Passages that are reasoning or generation (not retrieval) SHOULD be visually distinct or labeled to signal they are not cited.
constraints.rationale: Users conflate cited and uncited passages without distinction; labeling prevents false trust.
constraints.verification: Manual review: confirm uncited passages are styled or labeled differently from cited ones.

constraints.statement: The component MUST NOT cite the same source multiple times for identical claims; consolidate or re-phrase to avoid citation spam.
constraints.rationale: Redundant citations clutter the response and suggest the model is padding citations rather than reasoning.
constraints.verification: Unit test: registering the same source id twice yields one source-list entry referenced by both anchors.

wcagCriteria.name: Keyboard
wcagCriteria.relevance: Citation anchors and links must be keyboard-reachable and activatable.

wcagCriteria.name: Use of Color
wcagCriteria.relevance: Citations must not rely on color alone to distinguish them from surrounding text.

wcagCriteria.name: Name, Role, Value
wcagCriteria.relevance: Citation links must have accessible names and roles.

keyboard.action: Reaches each citation anchor and source link in document order.
Opens the source link or expands source metadata.

screenReader.behavior: Screen reader announces the cited text and that a source is available.
Screen reader announces the source title or URL.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focus moves naturally through citations in document order; no forced jumps.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Expand/collapse animations are disabled; regions appear instantly.

do: Use superscript numbers or brackets [1] for citations; they are universally understood.
Consolidate sources in a bibliography at the end; users often want to see all sources at once.
Show source metadata (date, domain) to help users judge credibility quickly.
dont: Do not force users to leave the page to see source metadata.
Do not cite opinion pieces or user-generated content as fact without labeling.
Do not cite the same source multiple times for the same claim.

references.title: Attributed Question Answering: Evaluation and Modeling for Attributed Large Language Models
references.note: Foundational work on evaluating whether generated answers are actually supported by their cited sources.
